history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row is the SAME temple as seq 874 (id rangji-temple-pushkar), which already documents the Old Rangji Temple (Purana Rangji Mandir) of Pushkar - commissioned by Seth Puranmal Ganeriwal of Hyderabad, date conflict 1823 vs 1844 flagged there too. Recommend removing this row or keeping 874 only. The Old Rangji Temple of Pushkar is a South-Indian (Dravidian)-style Vaishnavite temple, built by Seth Puran Mal Ganeriwala of Hyderabad - sources conflict on the date: 1823 (commissioned) vs 1844 (per testbook-style exam sources and a conservation report, verify which is correct). It is the first temple of the South-Indian Ramanuja Sampradaya in Rajasthan. The complex blends Dravidian, Rajput and Mughal styles, with a high-rising gopuram (125 ft, seven-tiered per one source - verify), shrines to Rangnath Venugopal/Krishna, Lakshmi and Ramanujacharya, plus a museum and Sheesh Mahal; the outer parikrama has ancient Ala-Gila (fresco) paintings and has been open to foreign tourists since 1864. NOTE: distinct from the larger Sri Rangji Temple at Vrindavan (existing id sri-rangji-temple-vrindavan) and the New Rangji temple at Pushkar - this row is the Old Rangji Mandir only.

town_description: Pushkar is a holy town in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, wrapped around the sacred Pushkar Lake, about 14 km northwest of Ajmer. Home to one of the few Brahma temples in the world plus hundreds of smaller shrines, it draws pilgrims year-round and peaks during the Pushkar Camel Fair (Kartik Purnima, Oct-Nov).
